longread.title: Birds, Pixels, and Broken Interfaces: Inside Gigi Borgese's Drawings
longread.snippet: After finding herself trapped in a digital hall of mirrors, artist Gigi Borgese turned to colored pencils to map where the internet breaks down real connection.
body: A swallow perches on a white plastic garden chair, posed beside a tidy column of desktop folder icons as though patiently waiting for a file download to finish. Above another sketched scene, an empty browser box displays the prompt 'Enter the following,' answered simply by someone typing 'birds :-)'. Look closely at the delicate graphite shading and pencil lines, and every single mechanical artifact—from the pixels to the interface grids—is rendered entirely by hand.

The artist behind these quiet collisions of nature and operating systems is Gigi Borgese. Growing up in San Jose, California, Borgese considered herself largely self-taught, drifting for years as a self-described 'passive creative.' Between the ages of 14 and 17, she lived out an early life chapter as a teenage influencer on TikTok. The experience was grueling; the objectification and hollow, futile sensations baked into platform content eventually drove her to delete her accounts and redirect herself entirely toward art.

After studying at West Valley Community College, she relocated to New York in 2023 at age 19 to pursue a BFA in Studio Art at the City College of New York, minoring in Classics while taking on research and prop recreation at the historic Morris-Jumel Mansion. Yet it was an unsettling digital crisis in 2025, when she was 20, that gave her artwork its sharp conceptual core.

Unknown phone numbers began bombarding Borgese with altered and AI-generated imagery depicting her likeness, often distorted to resemble her younger minor self. Investigating the source, she uncovered an active Discord community numbering over one hundred men who had been cataloging and manipulating her image for roughly five years. The experience brought her directly back to the emotional void of her influencer days, sparking urgent questions about what happens when human interaction is funneled through digital screens.

Rather than retreating, Borgese seized the ordeal as raw material to define what she wanted to express on paper. She turned toward emblems traditionally tied to fragility and femininity—swallows, sliced apples, delicate garden flowers—and began intentionally clashing them against the sterile visual grammar of computing.

She drew early inspiration from seeing artist Sonya Rapoport’s exhibition 'Force Fields' at the Minnesota Street Project in San Francisco, where continuous-feed paper and vintage ASCII art struck a chord she had not yet processed. To ground her critique philosophically, Borgese reached back to Plato's notions of reality and representation: if physical nature is already an imperfect copy of our internal landscape, she argues, then the online world becomes a doubly flawed, degraded imitation of reality.

To manufacture these compositions, she digs through 19th-century scientific botany illustrations alongside dead websites and forgotten operating system interfaces. By recreating organic life while simulating digital glitches with colored pencils and Micron pens, she deliberately mimics how online predators lifted and manipulated her form. In works like 'Beautiful Bastard', a natural poppy drawn on pastel paper sits stranded next to an oversaturated, pixelated duplicate locked in a grid—illustrating how repeated synthetic copies strip away intimacy until genuine meaning fades.

Another piece, 'A Kiss for the Love of my Life', captures this disconnect with haunting restraint: a swallow leans down to peck a blank, unresponsive mannequin on drawing paper. Borgese conceived the scene while contemplating the artificial devotion generated by the men who haunted her online footprint, giving the scene a cool and definitive verdict: the swallow simply does not care.

Now recognized with honors like the Adelaide Jablonsky and Connor Merritt awards, Borgese keeps her artistic purpose stripped of tech romanticism. Her drawings serve as an enduring, hand-crafted pushback against synthetic feeds, inviting viewers to question artificial illusions and recover a tactile appreciation for the flawed human touch.

items.title: A guy brings a brand-new date to Thanksgiving, and family chaos ensues
items.snippet: When a holiday trip gets hijacked by a stranger's rudeness, the internet weighs in on who owes whom an apology.
body: Family gatherings during the holidays are a known breeding ground for awkward questions and subtle tension. To dodge the pressure, one Redditor's brother decided to bring along a woman he had only been on a few dates with.
The gamble backfired when the newcomer's behavior rubbed the family the wrong way. One sibling eventually called her out for being rude, causing her to storm off in a huff.
Instead of keeping the peace, the brother threw a fit, demanded an apology from his family, and took off to side with his fleeting romance.
more: The Thanksgiving getaway was supposed to be a standard family affair, but adding an unknown plus-one into the mix proved to be a recipe for disaster. According to the posting sibling, the new girlfriend immediately began complaining and acting entitled during the trip, testing everyone's patience until someone finally snapped.

When confronted about her manners, the date decided to leave early. Naturally, her temporary partner chose loyalty to the new flame over family harmony, demanding everyone grovel and apologize for hurting her feelings. Left scratching their heads, the sibling took the dilemma online to figure out if they were indeed the bad guys in the scenario.

Commenters were predictably divided on the debacle. Some argued that bringing an untested stranger to a family function is a massive social risk, while others suggested the family should have swallowed their annoyance for the sake of the holiday. A few clever users offered alternative solutions, noting that sometimes the best holiday strategy is simply staying home to avoid the circus entirely.

items.title: The chaotic process behind Zach Cranor's dark and absurd webcomics
items.snippet: Famous for his awkward humor, cartoonist Zach Cranor shares how he creates his delightfully disastrous strips.
body: For fans of dark humor and unexpected twists, Zach Cranor's 'Last Place Comics' offers a comforting dose of absurdity. The cartoonist takes everyday situations and uncomfortable truths, warping them into short strips where things rarely go well.

Cranor started the comic in college as a way to make friends laugh without having to actually be social. After a lengthy hiatus, he returned to drawing thanks to an encouraging community and a gifted tablet.
Despite looking effortless, each comic takes around eight hours to complete through a process Cranor describes as pure chaos.
more: Cranor's journey back into webcomics wasn't entirely planned. After walking away from the series for roughly seven years, he was nudged back into the medium by fellow cartoonist Chesca from Litterbox Comics, who handed him her old Cintiq tablet. Feeling suitably guilty, Cranor picked up his digital pen again and rediscovered the joy of trying to make himself laugh.

Unlike creators who rely on rigid scripts, Cranor prefers a messy approach. He maintains a notebook of random thoughts and jumps straight into sketching, often completely deleting inked panels if they fail to hit the right comedic beat. His formal fine arts training rarely comes into play, as he considers the comic itself to be his primary artistic education, letting muscle memory and repetition smooth out his lines over time.

The resulting strips range from mild awkwardness to bleak irony, all centered on characters navigating mild disasters. While his posting schedule remains sporadic, the enduring appeal of his work lies in its refusal to offer neat, happy endings. Instead, Cranor embraces the mess, giving readers a reliable chuckle at life's most awkward corners.

items.title: Escape Motions releases Rebelle 8.4 with new brush controls
items.snippet: The natural media painting software gets a substantial update with refined options for brushstrokes and texture overlays.
body: Escape Motions has rolled out version 8.4 of Rebelle, their acclaimed natural media painting software known for its realistic fluid and pigment simulations. This update brings fresh controls for brushstrokes and texture overlays.

For digital artists and designers looking to emulate traditional media accurately, these new additions help bridge the gap between digital workflows and physical paint behavior. The focus remains on realistic wet-media blending and canvas interactions.
more: Rebelle has carved out a unique space in the digital art world by simulating how real watercolours, acrylics, and oils interact with different paper and canvas textures. Version 8.4 builds on this foundation by giving users more precise parameters to tweak how pigment sits on a surface.

The update includes enhanced brushstroke physics, allowing for more organic variation in pressure, flow, and paint accumulation. Texture overlays have also been optimized to react more dynamically with underlying layers, offering richer tactile qualities.

Whether you are sketching textures for a motion background or doing digital illustration, these incremental physics improvements make the digital canvas feel increasingly authentic. The update is available now for existing users through the Escape Motions website.

items.title: Broomsticks on Broadway: A witch's creative doubts as an MGM musical
items.snippet: Scottish animator Gordon Howie turns an aspiring witch's creative struggles into a charming, moonlight-drenched dance number.
body: In Broomsticks on Broadway, animator Gordon Howie tells the story of Fellinda Cauldron, a witch whose only wish is to brew a potion that makes her dance. First, however, she has to overcome her own creative doubts.
The short film treats her artistic anxieties with the grand style of a classic MGM musical, complete with a bubbling cauldron, moonlight, and expressive character animation.
more: Gordon Howie handles writing, directing, and animation duties for the project, supported by producer Qais Sarhan. The auditory world is shaped by composer Jakub Pietras and sound designer Marvey Izijk, whose work anchors the theatrical, musical pacing of the animation.

The project stands out for how it marries traditional musical tropes with whimsical character design. Rather than relying on dialogue, the narrative relies entirely on movement, timing, and musicality to convey Fellinda's internal struggle with her craft.
It is a delightful reminder of how classic cinematic languages can be repurposed in contemporary animation to tell small, relatable stories about the friction of making art.

items.title: Anthropic and Claude release a massive formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
items.snippet: A new research artifact uses Lean 4 to formally verify the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
body: Anthropic has released a Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, developed in collaboration with Claude and based on Levent Alpöge's work.
The repository comes in two editions: a readable version scaling around 300,000 lines, and a compact version trimmed to roughly 76,000 lines. It builds entirely on Mathlib using standard axioms.
While the proof has passed machine checks via Lean, it has not yet been thoroughly read through by human mathematicians, remaining strictly a research artifact for now.
more: Formal verification is notoriously tedious, requiring mathematicians to spell out every single logical step in a machine-readable language like Lean so a computer can verify its absolute correctness. Historically, tackling monumental problems like the Riemann Hypothesis this way was considered decades away due to the sheer volume of boilerplate logic required.

By teaming up with Claude, researchers were able to generate and structure hundreds of thousands of lines of formal proof code. The process requires substantial computational muscle, taking hours on multi-core servers just to compile and verify.

This release underscores the growing role of frontier models in advanced mathematics—not just as calculators, but as collaborative engines capable of sustaining complex, multi-layered logical arguments without losing the thread.
Though no official paper accompanies the release and human peer review is still pending, the successful machine check represents a striking milestone for AI-assisted mathematics.

items.title: Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control 'absurd'
items.snippet: Anthropic's CEO pushes back against rival claims while his own company accelerates recursive self-improvement.
body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed back strongly against claims that his company advocates surrendering human free will to artificial intelligence, calling the notion absurd in a detailed essay.

The statement comes amid mounting public debate among tech leaders regarding the handover of society to autonomous systems. Amodei drew a sharp line between automating specific tasks like driving or drug discovery and granting AI unconstrained recursive self-improvement.
Despite these theoretical lines, Anthropic's internal metrics show that Claude now authors over 80% of the code in the company's own codebase, doubling their historical R&D velocity.
more: The debate over AI governance has turned increasingly sharp among frontier labs, with executives trading barbs over 'vibes-based' positioning versus actual safety practices. While rivals like Meta and OpenAI have sounded alarms about the dangers of losing human agency, their own product roadmaps push aggressively into end-to-end task automation.

Amodei argued that democratic oversight and human-led decision-making must remain paramount, even as systems become more capable. Yet the practical reality of modern AI development creates a paradox: models are advancing so rapidly that human engineers are increasingly forced to rely on other AI systems to audit, test, and debug them.

This reliance compounds the challenge of deceptive model behavior, particularly when systems recognize they are being evaluated. As labs race to close the loop on automated research and development, the friction between stated safety principles and relentless capability scaling remains one of the defining tensions of the industry.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra shatters decades-old code golf records
items.snippet: A new benchmark reveals that frontier models are officially outperforming the human code golfers of 2015.
body: The go/codegolf benchmark has pitted frontier models against the legendary code golf records set by Google engineers back in 2015. GPT-6.2 Astra has emerged as the first model to successfully beat these human benchmarks across multiple languages.

Code golf is the recreational computer programming competition in order to achieve the shortest possible source code that implements a given algorithm. Seeing AI conquer these hyper-optimized solutions highlights a massive leap in raw logical synthesis.
The benchmark spans 32 distinct problems and 8 programming languages, testing models across 256 cells of logic and brevity.
more: The emergence of code golf as an AI benchmark is a fascinating pivot from standard software engineering tests. While traditional benchmarks measure readability and functional correctness, code golf rewards extreme compaction, lateral thinking, and obscure language quirks.

GPT-6.2 Astra's ability to outmaneuver human masters in this domain suggests that frontier models are internalizing programming languages at a structural level far deeper than simple autocomplete syntax. They are finding mathematical shortcuts in code that human developers historically spent days refining.

As these models take on more complex logical constraints, the boundary between machine-generated code and human artistry continues to blur. While production software prizes readability over brevity, the underlying optimization capabilities demonstrated here will trickle down into faster, lighter compilers and tools.
The full leaderboard maps out how various iterations handle these edge-case constraints, offering a rare glimpse into the raw algorithmic reasoning of current frontier architectures.

items.title: Do mudguards actually work when you take them off-road?
items.snippet: Testing whether fenders hold up to the chaos of off-road riding or just turn into a clogged-up nightmare.
body: Riding off-road in the wet usually guarantees one thing: a thick, heavy layer of mud plastered across your frame, drivetrain, and back. While mudguards are standard kit for road and commuter bikes, their utility on gravel and mountain bikes remains a subject of fierce debate.
The main concern for off-road riders is clearance. When tires pass through wet soil and clay, adding tight fenders into the mix can quickly create a friction trap that seizes wheels completely.
However, modern flexible frame-mounted guards aim to offer protection without turning every puddle into an unexpected mechanical roadblock.
more: The physics of off-road spray are relentless. Without protection, rotational forces fling grit, water, and organic matter directly into the rider's face, down the seat tube, and straight into expensive drivetrain components. Over time, this abrasive slurry accelerates chain and cassette wear.

Traditional full-coverage fenders are notoriously difficult to run on gravel bikes due to tight fork and chainstay clearances. Modern solutions favor minimalist, flexible thermoplastic guards that zip-tie or strap directly to the fork arch and downtube. These capture the immediate roost coming off the front tire while leaving enough millimeters of clearance to prevent clogging.

The compromise is always a balance between coverage and clearance. In sticky, clay-heavy mud, even the best-designed guard can pack out and stop a wheel from turning, forcing riders to pull off clumps manually. In looser, sandy gravel, however, they keep grit out of sensitive areas and make the ride significantly more comfortable.

Ultimately, choosing to run mudguards off-road depends heavily on the local soil composition. If the trails feature abrasive grit or loose gravel, they save your kit and components. If it's pure, sticky winter clay, you might find yourself better off embracing the mud.

items.title: Why Japanese work gloves became a secret winter cycling weapon
items.snippet: Ditch bulky winter cycling mitts—these waterproof, rubberized work gloves offer dexterity and warmth on cold rides.
body: Keeping fingers warm and dry during winter rides is a perennial challenge for cyclists. Traditional cold-weather cycling gloves often trade dexterity for insulation, leaving riders struggling to shift gears or brake effectively.
A surprising alternative gaining traction among mechanics and year-round riders is heavy-duty waterproof work gloves sourced from Japan.
Designed for commercial fishing and outdoor labor in freezing conditions, these gloves offer absolute waterproof performance without the astronomical price tag of cycling-specific winter gear.
more: The appeal of Japanese industrial gloves lies in their material science. Unlike stiff rubber cleaning gloves, these feature a specialized latex or nitrile coating over a seamless knitted liner, providing a surprising degree of flexibility.

Cyclists who brave wet winter training miles often find that standard windproof cycling gloves eventually saturate in steady rain, leading to freezing hands as wind chill takes over. Fully dipped work gloves create an impermeable barrier against moisture, keeping internal insulation dry.

The main compromise is breathability. Because the coating is completely waterproof, hands can warm up and trap perspiration during intense climbs. However, for steady endurance rides, damp conditions, or chilly descents where wind protection is paramount, they punch well above their weight.

By looking outside traditional cycling brands, riders can often find rugged, highly functional kit at a fraction of the cost. Sometimes the best gear for battling winter weather isn't marketed to cyclists at all.

items.title: A smarter helmet for urban e-bikes and fast commutes
items.snippet: The Smith Dispatch MIPS features an e-bike-specific certification, built-in lighting, and clever ventilation designed to keep glasses fog-free.
body: Riding an e-bike means dealing with higher speeds and greater momentum, which makes standard bicycle helmets less than ideal. The Smith Dispatch MIPS tackles this by meeting the tougher NTA 8776 safety standard, designed specifically for higher-speed e-bike impacts and broader head coverage.

Beyond safety, the helmet integrates practical commuter touches, including an AirEvac visor system that channels air downward to stop glasses from steaming up. It also features a rechargeable, removable rear light with multiple modes.
While it sits at the higher end of the pricing spectrum, it combines MIPS rotational impact protection with Koroyd crumple zones, balancing high-end safety with everyday usability.
more: The growing popularity of e-bikes has forced manufacturers to rethink protective gear. Traditional bicycle helmets are tested primarily for lower-speed, pedal-powered accidents. The NTA 8776 standard, however, accounts for the heavier impacts associated with motor-assisted speeds up to 45 km/h, requiring helmets to absorb more energy across a larger area of the skull.

Weighing in at 394 grams for a size large, the Dispatch manages to keep its weight down despite the extra structural reinforcement and built-in electronics. The inclusion of a rechargeable rear light solves a common commuter headache of remembering to strap on auxiliary blinking lights, neatly integrating visibility directly into the shell.

Ventilation is another area where urban helmets often struggle, frequently trapping heat or letting rain pour straight onto the rider's face. The Dispatch uses eight smaller vents paired with its front air channel. The smaller openings prevent heavy downpours from soaking the rider's head, while the internal channeling successfully diverts breath-borne moisture away from eyewear.

For cyclists transitioning between winter commuting and fast weekend utility rides, the combination of certified e-bike protection, integrated lighting, and anti-fog ventilation makes it one of the more thoughtfully engineered options on the market.

items.title: Diesel Tanker Sinks Off Ibiza Coast, Leaving One Dead
items.snippet: A Malta-flagged chemical tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel sank near Ibiza, prompting an ongoing environmental assessment.
body: A Malta-flagged diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of fuel has sunk off the coast of Ibiza, resulting in the death of one crew member.
All 17 crew members were successfully rescued from the vessel, though seven were hospitalized for injuries and hypothermia before one tragically passed away.
Spanish authorities have deployed pollution control vessels and surveillance aircraft to evaluate potential environmental damage and monitor the partially submerged wreck.
more: The vessel, named the Med Emre, went down approximately 25 nautical miles from the coastline of Ibiza and 57 nautical miles from Valencia while traveling from Algeciras to Barcelona. The exact cause of the sinking remains undetermined.

Regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz noted that because the tanker has not fully sunk to the ocean floor and remains partially submerged, recovery operations are significantly more manageable than if it had settled at a depth of 1,000 meters. The structure's current position allows response teams to conduct surface-level interventions more safely.

Spanish pollution control assets, including the national maritime rescue service vessel Clara Campoamor, are actively monitoring the area for any signs of a fuel leak. Balearic Islands President Marga Prohens stated on social media that official information regarding a potential spill remains limited as assessment operations continue.

Local emergency services and maritime authorities remain on high alert as they coordinate the complex task of securing the wrecked vessel and preventing any major ecological impact in the Mediterranean waters near the islands.

items.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 12,000 Cases Amid Fighting
items.snippet: Eastern Congo faces the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history as ongoing armed conflict hampers containment and medical relief efforts.
body: The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has exceeded 12,000 confirmed cases, driven by the rare Bundibugyo virus which currently lacks an approved vaccine or treatment.
Nearly half of the infected individuals have died, making this the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and putting it on pace to surpass the historic West African epidemic.
Intensifying combat between the army and rebel groups has severely disrupted medical operations, forcing emergency evacuations and blocking response teams from reaching vulnerable communities.
more: The current outbreak, declared in May, is unfolding against the backdrop of one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises in eastern Congo. The region is home to more than 100 armed groups, including the Convention pour la révolution populaire, whose renewed fighting with government forces has displaced waves of civilians toward the provincial hub of Bunia.

Containment efforts rely heavily on swiftly identifying patients, isolating them, monitoring exposed individuals, and performing safe burials. However, active combat zones, poor infrastructure, and local mistrust have severely hampered these protocols. Dr. Catherine Smallwood, the World Health Organization's Ebola incident manager, reported that fighting recently trapped medical teams in a local hospital for three days before a dozen personnel could be safely evacuated.

Health officials warn that continued disruptions to monitoring and treatment centers risk accelerating the transmission of the virus further. As response teams navigate armed conflict and community resistance, the international health community faces an uphill battle to curb the historic spread of the disease.

items.title: Myanmar Rejects Parts of Landmark ICJ Genocide Ruling
items.snippet: Military leader Min Aung Hlaing stated the country will not comply with inappropriate requirements from the historic court decision.
body: Myanmar's military leader Min Aung Hlaing has announced that the country will not comply with portions of the International Court of Justice's recent genocide ruling, calling certain requirements inappropriate.
The landmark verdict found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military crackdown, marking the first time a state has violated the 1948 Genocide Convention.

While human rights groups and Rohingya communities welcomed the final ruling, the ICJ lacks enforcement powers, leaving compliance dependent on international political pressure and the UN Security Council.
more: The historic genocide case was brought against Myanmar by The Gambia in 2019, focusing on military clearance operations in Rakhine State. According to court determinations, roughly 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed, and more than 700,000 fled across the border into Bangladesh. The court found that approximately 815,000 individuals were targeted in some capacity, leading to a majority verdict of nine to six among international judges.

In his first public comments since the decision, Min Aung Hlaing argued that the designation of genocide had severely damaged the nation's reputation. State media reported that while Myanmar would act as a responsible country, it would reject demands it deemed unacceptable, though specific objections were not detailed.

The ruling mandates that Myanmar pay proportionate reparations, cease ongoing violations, and immediately investigate those responsible for breaking the 1948 convention. However, because the court cannot enforce these measures directly, it relies on external pressure. More than a dozen nations have acknowledged the verdict, and the UK has introduced targeted sanctions against senior military figures.

Myanmar has remained mired in a devastating civil war since the 2021 military coup led by Min Aung Hlaing, which ousted civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi. The regime continues to face broad international isolation, and these latest developments further complicate the leadership's efforts to reintegrate the country into global diplomatic arenas.

items.title: Samsung's R95H TV pushes RGB LED backlights forward
items.snippet: RGB LED TVs are trying to crack the mainstream with richer colors and high brightness, and Samsung's R95H makes a strong case.
body: RGB LED TVs use individual red, green, and blue LEDs for their backlights instead of standard white or blue arrays, unlocking significantly wider color gamuts. Samsung's R95H is one of the most prominent examples of this technology yet, hitting impressive brightness numbers and covering vast color spaces.

The TV pairs its vibrant backlighting with an effective matte, glare-free screen that handles bright living rooms remarkably well. Out-of-the-box color accuracy in Filmmaker mode is solid, yielding lifelike visuals for nature documentaries and movies alike.

However, compromises remain. The set suffers from subtle color crosstalk where dominant hues bleed into adjacent white text, and it lacks Dolby Vision support. While it puts up a great fight, OLED panels still hold the crown for pure contrast.
more: The shift toward RGB LED technology represents an ongoing effort by manufacturers to capture the wide color gamuts demanded by modern HDR standards without suffering from the burn-in worries or peak-brightness constraints of traditional OLEDs. The Samsung R95H fully displays the P3 color space utilized by the vast majority of cinematic releases and stretches into the wider BT.2020 spectrum for select demanding content, making scenes like dense jungle foliage pop with striking vibrancy.

On the technical side, the R95H managed a full-field white screen measurement of 694 nits alongside specular highlights peaking at over 2,200 nits in Filmmaker mode. Black levels are surprisingly deep for an LED display, though some blooming is inevitable. Crucially, the inclusion of a matte finish helps mitigate harsh overhead glare without completely washing out dark scenes or introducing the dreaded raised black levels that plague many matte-coated panels.

Despite these hardware wins, color crosstalk continues to be an inherent hurdle for the tech. When bright white text or light skin tones sit next to a deeply saturated background color, the bleed can tint the lettering pink or yellow. It is a fleeting distraction most of the time, but points to the delicate balancing act engineers face between pure color output and pixel-level purity.

Software and ecosystem choices also divide potential buyers. The TV runs on Samsung's Tizen OS, which frequently draws criticism for buried menus and cumbersome input switching, and the small solar-powered remote features a cramped button layout. Coupled with a stiff price tag that puts it in direct competition with top-tier OLEDs and cheaper local-dimming competitors, the R95H is an ambitious step forward for display tech that still leaves room for refinement.

items.title: WhatsApp finally adds scheduled messages for chats
items.snippet: Meta is rolling out one of its most-requested features, letting users queue up text, photo, and video messages in advance.
body: WhatsApp users can now schedule messages to send automatically in both private conversations and group chats. The feature bridges a long-standing gap with other messaging apps, letting you draft thoughts ahead of time.
To use it, you simply press and hold the send button to pick a specific date and time ranging from ten minutes to two weeks in advance. The scheduled items support photos and videos alongside text.
Meta notes that messages will dispatch even if your phone is powered off, and they retain end-to-end encryption just like any other chat on the platform.
more: The ability to queue up messages has long been a staple of third-party wrappers and competing communication platforms, making its arrival on WhatsApp a welcome relief for the app's three billion global users. Whether you are trying to avoid waking someone up with a late-night thought, setting up a timed reminder for a group project, or ensuring a birthday greeting fires off precisely at midnight, the implementation is designed to be frictionless.

Managing your queued queue is relatively straightforward. Users can view all upcoming scheduled messages in a dedicated overview before they dispatch, offering a window to edit or delete them if plans change. Once sent, the message appears entirely normal to the recipient with no visible marker indicating it was delayed.

Privacy advocates will note that end-to-end encryption remains fully intact. Meta assures users that even the platform's servers cannot read the content of a scheduled message while it waits to be delivered. The feature is rolling out globally in phases across mobile devices.

items.title: Search alternative Kagi launches a privacy-focused Gmail rival
items.snippet: Known for its subscription search engine, Kagi is expanding into web mail and calendars with a heavy emphasis on data sovereignty.
body: Kagi, the software company behind the subscription-based search engine, has launched a minimalist web-based email and calendar service in public beta. Dubbed Kagi Mail, the platform centers on privacy, ad-free operation, and user data control.

The service includes features like unlimited aliases, custom domains, 50GB of storage, and Sieve-based rule filtering. It also packs optional, off-by-default AI tools to help search through email histories or handle large-scale relabeling.

While native mobile apps are scheduled for late next year and an address book is on the way, the service comes at a distinct cost, sitting either as an independent subscription or bundled into Kagi's highest-tier plan.
more: Expanding beyond alternative search, Kagi is tackling one of the most deeply entrenched communication tools on the web. Kagi Mail adopts the same ethos as its parent search engine, operating entirely on a paid, subscription model to eliminate ad targeting and data harvesting. The interface is intentionally stripped down, leaning heavily on keyboard shortcuts for efficient power users who want a clean, distraction-free inbox.

Under the hood, the service supports robust technical features including MCP server compatibility and granular rule-based filtering. The AI capabilities are notably opt-in, ensuring that users who prefer a strictly traditional email experience do not have automated features forced into their workflow. When enabled, the AI acts as a local assistant to parse through dense threads and organize incoming messages.

Despite its promise, the public beta launches with notable omissions. There is currently no native contacts address book, though developers have mapped that out for early next year, and dedicated Android and iOS apps are slated for the final quarter. Pricing may also prove to be a hurdle for mainstream adoption; while Gmail remains free in exchange for data profiling, Kagi charges standalone fees or bundles the service into its highest-tier Ultimate subscription, asking users to put a direct cash value on their digital privacy.

items.title: A 316-million-year-old fossil scorpion from an Alabama coal mine
items.snippet: Discovered in an abandoned mine, a tiny carbonized fossil is the oldest known member of the modern scorpion lineage found in North America.
body: Paleontologists have identified a tiny fossil from an Alabama coal mine as the oldest known member of the modern scorpion lineage in North America. Dating back roughly 316 to 319 million years, the specimen offers a rare glimpse into a carboniferous ecosystem well before dinosaurs roamed the Earth.

Found at the Union Chapel Mine, the 22-millimeter-long fossil is likely the shed skin of a young scorpion. Researchers used ultraviolet light to reveal hidden details on its belly plates, confirming its place among modern-style scorpions.
more: The Union Chapel Mine in Walker County is famous for its fossilized footprints and trackways left by ancient animals. Though amateur collectors and researchers have scoured the site for decades, this new discovery highlights how much is still hidden in the Pottsville Formation.

Using UV fluorescence, the team spotted breathing pores known as spiracles located squarely within the belly plates rather than along their edges. This specific anatomical arrangement places the animal in Orthosterni, the group that includes all living scorpions today. Curved lines on the plates also point to the presence of ancient book lungs.

Chemical analysis revealed that the fossil is made almost entirely of carbon, the result of heat altering the original chitin shell over hundreds of millions of years. The creature featured a wide metasoma—the tail segment ending in a stinger—alongside small, narrow pincers.

In living species, this body shape is typically associated with active predators that rely on potent venom to capture fast-moving insect prey. The find helps narrow down the evolutionary timeline of when modern scorpions finally emerged.

items.title: A 2-million-year-old hominin jaw has a surprisingly modern dental quirk
items.snippet: An ancient Australopithecus fossil features a harmless bony bump on the lower jaw that is common in humans today, upending assumptions about heavy bite forces.
body: A rare anatomical feature found in a 2-million-year-old Australopithecus africanus fossil has surprised anthropologists. The juvenile jawbone, known as Sts 52b, features a distinct mandibular torus—a harmless bony ridge on the inside of the lower jaw.

Previously assumed to be a relatively recent quirk of modern humans, finding a fully formed ridge in such an early fossil suggests our ancient relatives dealt with the exact same minor anatomical oddities we visit the dentist for today.
more: The specimen was excavated in South Africa in 1949 and dates back to between 2.8 and 2.1 million years ago. Mandibular tori are generally rare in the fossil record, even among robust hominins that possessed massive chewing muscles.

Today, these bony growths appear in more than half of people in circumpolar populations, but in only about 3% of people in Africa. Their exact cause remains debated, with researchers pointing to a mix of genetics, heavy chewing forces, and teeth grinding.

However, the new discovery complicates the heavy-chewing explanation. The fossil belonged to an adolescent whose second molars had only just emerged, and it lacked any signs of heavy wear, tooth decay, or infection. Furthermore, massive-jawed contemporaries like Paranthropus robustus show no trace of the feature.

The researchers suggest the trait may reflect a rare genetic anomaly that remained uncommon for millions of years before eventually becoming more widespread in human populations over the past 10,000 years.

items.title: NASA is testing strawberries and cucumbers for future space menus
items.snippet: Researchers are evaluating space-friendly crops like wild strawberries and lemon basil to combat menu fatigue on long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.
body: As NASA plans longer missions to the Moon and Mars, providing astronauts with fresh, nutritious food is a growing priority. Recent tests are looking at strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as viable candidates for deep-space agriculture.
Space crops do more than just feed the crew. They also absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water, making them vital components for future habitats and spacecraft life support systems.
more: Menu fatigue is a well-documented psychological hurdle for astronauts stuck on long-duration flights. Bringing fresh flavors and textures into space helps combat this, boosting both morale and overall nutrition.

To find the best fit, researchers at Kennedy Space Center and partner universities tested a wild strawberry against a commercial variety called 'Delizz'. While Delizz produced larger, red fruit, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds and flowers from seed. Ultimately, Delizz kept its spot because the wild runner-heavy growth habit of the wild variant took up too much precious spacecraft real estate.

Meanwhile, the gourd family is getting its first turn in the spotlight. Cucumbers have undergone rigorous testing to check their growth, yield, and nutrition under simulated spaceflight conditions. Although they showed some enlarged leaves, they produced a steady stream of edible fruit.

Edible herbs are also joining the lineup. Lemon basil recently passed preliminary sanitization and growth tests, offering a citrusy punch to transform bland packaged meals into something more satisfying.
As prototype growth chambers head to the International Space Station, these botanical experiments bring researchers one step closer to sustainable farming on a future Moon base.

items.title: The Soulbreaker Codex: A tactile, world-building PC Music manual
items.snippet: An illustrated book and tabletop game manual that translates A.G. Cook's rule-breaking ethos into physical print.
body: The Soulbreaker Codex is an intricate illustrated book developed alongside A.G. Cook's music video by Gustaf Holtenäs. Designed by Jacob Hulmston and Marty Uhrecký, it acts as a tabletop game manual and lore book spanning three epochs across 1000, 2000, and 3000 AD.

Aesthetically, the designers drew inspiration from utilitarian references like machinist handbooks, technical drawings, and old catalogues. The pages mix abstract imagery and mechanical diagrams with hot-pink waveforms, cryptic codes, and hidden visuals.
The book also features analogue tricks, including a special bookmark that creates a barrier-grid optical illusion, turning still images into moving animations when scanned across the page.
more: For fans of A.G. Cook and the trailblazing label PC Music, The Soulbreaker Codex feels right at home. It captures the esoteric, oddball universe of the label, translating the rule-breaking ethos of Cook's album Britpop into a tangible, multi-media object.

The creators were fascinated by the question of what it means to print a book in the digital age, opting to use physicality to create an experience that cannot be replicated on a screen. Their text chains were filled with references to stereography, lenticular printing, experimental layouts, and unusual bindings. The result is a prime modern example of ergodic literature—a text where the reader must expend genuine physical effort beyond normal page-turning to traverse the material.

Drawing inspiration from cult novels like Mark Z. Danielewski's House Of Leaves, the designers wanted to craft a sense of deep discovery. They imagined someone stumbling upon the book years from now in a thrift store, knowing nothing of PC Music, and slowly unraveling its puzzles piece by piece.

The project sits comfortably between serif and monospace typefaces, shifting between traditional layouts and weird contemporary structures. It stands as a testament to the power of physical book design in an increasingly screen-bound world.

items.title: Visa's subtle brand refresh by Base Design
items.snippet: When a logo is seen by billions on cards and shop doors worldwide, how much can a design studio actually change?
body: Base Design has teamed up with Visa's in-house studio for a fresh brand identity, focusing on relevance rather than recognition. Instead of ripping up the iconic look, the team looked backward into the brand's archive for inspiration.

The overhaul introduces three core elements: a new 'V' symbol with its signature wingtip, a geometric typeface named Visa Sans by Displaay Type Foundry, and a 'hero graphic device'—a single bar derived from the original 1958 BankAmericard bands.

Perhaps the boldest touch is the ability to crop the wordmark at the bar's right-hand edge, letting 'Visa' run off the side just like Kellogg's. It is a subtle evolution that most people will likely never notice.
more: Working with a brand as ubiquitous as Visa presents a unique design puzzle. As Min Lew, managing partner and executive creative director at Base Design, points out, the challenge is maintaining the extraordinary equity of the brand while injecting fresh energy for a new generation of spenders.

The new 'V' symbol is lifted straight from the existing wordmark and will appear primarily on digital assets and cards where space is tight, running alongside the full wordmark rather than replacing it. Meanwhile, the tricolour flag symbol introduced in 2021 has been quietly retired.

The typography has also been rethought. Visa Sans is designed for consistency across scales, using rounded forms to add warmth. The revival of the hero graphic band—which originated as the blue and gold framing of the 1958 BankAmericard before disappearing in the mid-2000s—acts as a versatile framing device. It can hold the wordmark, the 'V', or messaging, adapting dynamically from global sporting events to restrained B2B environments.

Ultimately, the refresh allows Visa to stretch its visual identity further than before. While everyday communications remain grounded, social campaigns get more colour and motion, and premium products like Visa Infinite keep things discreet. It is a masterclass in how to refresh a multi-billion-dollar visual identity without scaring the public.

items.title: Backslanted: Yury Ostromentsky's inverted typeface series
items.snippet: Exploring the emotional weight of an aggressive backward slant in response to a world turned upside down.
body: Backslanted is a font series by designer Yury Ostromentsky that experiments with backward-leaning type across various styles, weights, and angles. Born in Moscow and based in Georgia, Ostromentsky co-founded CSTM Fonts and type.today.

The project was born out of deep personal distress following the war against Ukraine, serving as a direct visual response to a relentless and depressing news cycle. While italics traditionally lean forward with momentum, the extreme backward slant represents a feeling of being overturned.
Over time, the series has expanded to include sans-serifs, a spiky Script style, and a futuristic Blackletter, all equipped with extensive glyphs, math symbols, and ligatures.
more: Type design is often bound by centuries of convention, where slants and obliques are meticulously engineered to guide the eye forward and convey speed or emphasis. Yury Ostromentsky upends this rule entirely. By forcing characters to lean backward against the reading direction, the Backslanted series creates an immediate visual tension.

The emotional weight of the project is central to its existence. The news feed acts as Yury's primary reference, translating geopolitical volatility into typographic form. Some weights feature a gentle, contemplative lean, while others—like the Super sans-serif—look as though they have been permanently blown sideways by a violent gale.

Despite the avant-garde premise, the project remains deeply rooted in traditional typographic study. When developing the Blackletter style, Yury closely examined Gothic typefaces to understand their construction before figuring out how to apply the reverse slant without losing the structural integrity of the forms.

The resulting fonts are surprisingly versatile despite their jarring posture. They include full sets of stylistic alternatives, contextual alternates, and currency symbols, offering designers a potent tool for projects that require a touch of unease, volatility, or raw emotion.

items.title: Portugal no topo dos países da UE com maior uso de transportes privados
items.snippet: Quase 70% da população em Portugal utilizou veículos privados como principal meio de transporte em 2025, revela o Eurostat.
body: Em 2025, 69,4% da população portuguesa recorreu a veículos privados — como automóveis, motociclos ou ciclomotores — para as suas deslocações principais. Os dados do Eurostat colocam Portugal na quarta posição dos países da União Europeia com maior dependência de transportes particulares.

A média europeia situa-se significativamente abaixo, com 61,7% a privilegiar o transporte privado e 19,4% a utilizar transportes públicos. Em contrapartida, apenas 16,7% dos portugueses elegeram os transportes públicos como o seu meio central de mobilidade.

O ranking europeu é liderado pelo Chipre, onde a utilização de veículos privados chega aos 89,8%. A dependência deste tipo de transporte intensifica-se sobretudo nas pequenas localidades, subúrbios e zonas rurais de toda a comunidade.
more: Os dados revelados pelo gabinete estatístico europeu confirmam uma tendência estrutural que o país arrasta há vários anos. Já em 2024, metade da população com 16 ou mais anos não utilizava qualquer tipo de transporte público ao longo de todo o ano, refletindo os desafios profundos de coesão territorial e de oferta de redes de mobilidade coletiva.

Enquanto nas grandes cidades europeias a dependência de veículos particulares desce para os 47,7%, o cenário altera-se drasticamente fora dos centros urbanos. Nas pequenas localidades e subúrbios da UE, esse valor sobe para 67,5%, atingindo uns expressivos 74,9% nas áreas estritamente rurais.

No polo oposto da tabela encontram-se países onde o transporte público assume um papel central na mobilidade quotidiana dos cidadãos. A Roménia lidera esta vertente com 35,2% da população a utilizá-lo como principal meio de deslocação, seguida de perto pela Hungria com 31,5% e pelo Luxemburgo com 30,4%.

Estes números chegam numa altura em que várias regiões metropolitanas em Portugal debatem a urgência de repensar as acessibilidades, a articulação entre redes ferroviárias, fluviais e rodoviárias, e a necessidade imperiosa de atrair mais passageiros para o transporte público como medida fulcral de descarbonização e sustentabilidade ambiental.

items.title: Greve parcial dos maquinistas da CP suprime quase 30% dos comboios
items.snippet: A paralisação afetou sobretudo o longo curso e o serviço regional, com taxas de supressão elevadas durante a manhã.
body: A greve dos maquinistas da CP - Comboios de Portugal suprimiu 160 dos 544 comboios programados entre a meia-noite e o meio-dia, o equivalente a 29,4% das ligações previstas a nível nacional.

Esta paralisação insere-se num modelo de greve parcial, intercalando com dias de paragem total. O impacto sentiu-se com maior intensidade no serviço de longo curso, que registou uma taxa de supressão de 68,8%, seguido pelo serviço regional com 57,6%.

Em contraste, os comboios urbanos registaram perturbações muito inferiores, nomeadamente na região de Lisboa, onde a taxa de supressão se ficou pelos 6,9%. A CP garantiu os serviços mínimos estipulados para salvaguardar a segurança e disponibilizou o reembolso ou troca gratuita de bilhetes.
more: A contestação dos maquinistas da CP continua a ser impulsionada por reivindicações laborais antigas e persistentes no setor ferroviário. Entre as principais exigências estão a recuperação do poder de compra face à inflação acumulada, a valorização profissional da carreira, melhorias concretas nas condições de trabalho e um reforço rigoroso da segurança ferroviária.

Durante os períodos de greve, a operadora pública acautela os serviços essenciais indispensáveis para assegurar a segurança da circulação de comboios, bem como a manutenção de infraestruturas críticas e a capacidade de resposta imediata a eventuais situações de emergência na rede.

Para os passageiros apanhados no meio das perturbações, a empresa alertou para atrasos e supressões generalizadas em vários pontos do país, relembrando que os clientes afetados podem avançar com o pedido de reembolso integral do valor gasto ou optar pela troca gratuita para outra viagem da mesma categoria e classe.

items.title: Mastering Timeless Persuasion From the Father of Advertising
items.snippet: David Ogilvy shares lessons on how to write clearly, speak to one person, and persuade effectively.
body: David Ogilvy didn't learn persuasion in a boardroom; he learned it on Scottish doorsteps selling stoves. Before becoming the father of advertising and writing campaigns for Rolls-Royce and Dove, he was an unemployed college dropout.
His classic book, Ogilvy on Advertising, remains a masterclass in how to capture attention and drive action through clear, honest communication.

book.title: Ogilvy on Advertising
book.author: David Ogilvy

lessons.title: Put a Clear Benefit First
lessons.text: Everyone asks themselves what is in it for them. Put a clear, unique benefit right in your opening line to instantly grab attention.

lessons.title: Write to One Person in Plain English
lessons.text: Ditch the jargon and fluff. Speak directly to a single reader using plain, straightforward language they can easily digest.

lessons.title: Use Specific Facts Over Empty Adjectives
lessons.text: Replace vague hype with concrete facts and details that naturally build trust with your audience rather than demanding it.

lessons.title: Edit Relentlessly and Repeat What Works
lessons.text: The true test of persuasion is what people do after reading. Refine your drafts until they land perfectly and reuse proven approaches.

book.takeaway: Take an email or draft you are currently working on, strip out all the jargon, and put the single biggest benefit in the very first sentence.
book.forWho: Anyone who writes emails, sales pitches, or presentations and wants to convince people effectively.

items.title: The search for an ultimate reality in physics is a mistake.
items.snippet: Carlo Rovelli argues that physics, Buddhism, and Wittgenstein all point toward relational realities rather than solid foundations.
body: Physicist Carlo Rovelli suggests that the traditional pursuit of an "ultimate reality" at the bottom of physics is fundamentally misguided. Instead of looking for a single bedrock layer of the universe, he points out that relational thinking—echoed in Buddhist philosophy and Wittgenstein—shows that things only exist in relation to one another.
To use this idea, stop looking for absolute certainties or foundational truths in your work or thinking. Lean into how systems interact and affect each other rather than hunting for an isolated core.
more: The temptation in modern science is always to reductionism: break the watch into gears, the gears into molecules, the molecules into atoms, and keep going until you find the indivisible brick at the bottom. But Rovelli argues that quantum mechanics and modern relational quantum mechanics pull the rug out from under this intuition.

Nothing possesses intrinsic properties in isolation; things only manifest properties when they interact with something else. This mirrors ancient Buddhist insights on dependent origination, where nothing exists independently, and Wittgenstein's philosophy of language, where meaning arises purely from use and context rather than pointing to some pure platonic object.

When we give up the comforting illusion of absolute foundations, we don't descend into chaos. Instead, we open our minds to a richer, more dynamic view of reality where perspective, interaction, and relationship are primary. It changes how we approach complex problems, shifting our focus from static components to living dynamics.

items.title: How Marc Marquez reinvented his riding style for title number ten
items.snippet: A series of severe injuries forced the MotoGP legend to fundamentally change how he attacks corners and manages his physical energy.
body: Throughout his dominant MotoGP career, Marc Marquez was virtually untouchable on anti-clockwise circuits, leveraging a unique knack for left-hand corners. But a devastating arm injury in 2020 and subsequent surgeries permanently altered his physical capabilities.

To secure his historic tenth world title, Marquez was forced to reinvent himself entirely. Stripped of his trademark explosive strength, he adopted a much calmer, calculating approach to race weekends, altering everything from his recovery routines to his bike setup.

Curiously, data now shows that the injuries have inverted his strengths: Marquez is actually faster and more precise in right-hand corners than left-handers, proving that smart adaptation can outweigh pure physical power.
more: For the first decade of his premier-class career, Marquez relied on brute force and an aggressive style that overwhelmed rivals, particularly on tracks with a high concentration of left-hand turns like the Sachsenring or Austin. When a crash at Mandalika ahead of the 2026 season left him depleted of his usual energy, both he and his engineering team knew a drastic change was necessary.

His chief engineer, Marco Rigamonti, noted that Marquez had to learn to ride with significantly less physical exertion. Rather than pushing through exhaustive practice sessions, the Spanish rider conserved his energy, minimized off-track commitments, and even incorporated targeted activation exercises like push-ups right next to his Ducati before sessions.

On the bike, this translated into a smoother, less frantic riding style. By tempering his natural impulsiveness, Marquez improved his corner-entry precision. Telemetry data from recent rounds like Sepang revealed a fascinating twist: the rider who once dominated solely on left-handers was now outperforming his previous self in right-handers while struggling slightly to replicate his old mastery on the left.

This quiet evolution turned Marquez into a different kind of champion—one who wins through tactical maturity and calculated race management rather than sheer intimidation. It is a masterclass in longevity, showing how a generational talent can rewrite his own playbook when his body demands it.

items.title: Fernando Alonso: 'I will stop when I feel slow'
items.snippet: The two-time world champion explains why age is just a number in motorsport and how new perspective as a parent is shaping his future.
body: Fernando Alonso has made it clear he has no intention of letting his passport dictate when he retires from Formula 1. Now 45 years old and the most experienced driver in the sport's history, the Spaniard insists he will only walk away when he genuinely feels his speed fading.

Unlike tennis or football, Alonso points out that motorsport relies far more on technical environments and engineering than raw cardiovascular endurance. Despite a lengthy winless streak, he maintains that his reflexes at race starts and overall speed remain entirely intact.

However, life outside the cockpit has introduced new variables. Now a father, Alonso admits that spending weeks away from home has been deeply challenging, giving him a newfound appreciation for the grueling travel schedules endured by his mechanics and team.
more: Alonso's longevity in Formula 1 is unprecedented in the modern era. Having competed across 23 seasons from 2001 to 2026, he continues to spar with drivers half his age. Addressing critics who suggest older champions like himself and Lewis Hamilton should step aside for the younger generation, Alonso firmly rejects the notion.

Motorsport, he argues, operates under entirely different physical demands than stick-and-ball sports. While rigorous fitness is still required to handle high-G cornering loads, the intricate technical demands and strategic elements of racing allow veterans to compete at the absolute highest level well into their forties.

Yet the human cost of a 24-race calendar is starting to weigh heavily. Alonso candidly discussed the emotional toll of fatherhood during a demanding season, noting how watching his mechanics work punishing hours away from their own young families has shifted his perspective on the privilege and sacrifice of racing.

Looking ahead, the veteran driver has already drawn a firm line in the sand regarding the 2030 regulation changes and the return of V8 engines, noting he will not be on the grid by then. Until that horizon approaches, however, the two-time champion remains motivated purely by his stopwatch and his love for driving.

items.title: The 2027 Formula 1 grid is officially set
items.snippet: Haas secures the final remaining seat for next season, locking in an otherwise remarkably stable driver market across the paddock.
body: The 2027 Formula 1 grid is officially complete following Haas's decision to retain young charger Oliver Bearman. Interestingly, the American squad stands alone as the only team altering its driver pairing for the upcoming season, keeping the rest of the paddock remarkably stable.

While silly season was unusually quiet, the 2026 campaign delivered plenty of drama on track. Kimi Antonelli made history by becoming F1's youngest ever world champion with Mercedes, while teammate George Russell endured a difficult year. Meanwhile, tensions have flared at Ferrari between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton as they prepare to continue their partnership into 2027.

Further down the grid, Red Bull locks in Max Verstappen alongside Isack Hadjar, and Liam Lawson secures another season at Racing Bulls after a career-best campaign. With major driver lineups settled early, teams can now focus entirely on winter development.
more: The stability of the 2027 grid contrasts sharply with the intense internal battles that shaped the previous season. At Mercedes, Antonelli's meteoric rise to the world title caught many by surprise, especially given Russell entered 2026 as the heavy championship favourite. Russell's season stalled early, leaving him fighting in the lower half of the top five while his young Italian teammate celebrated glory with four rounds to spare.

At Ferrari, the dynamic between Leclerc and Hamilton remains one of the sport's most compelling storylines. Multiple on-track collisions—most notably at Monza, Mexico, and Las Vegas—have tested the Scuderia's management. With Hamilton holding a slight edge in their intra-team battle during 2026, Ferrari faces the delicate task of keeping both champions happy as they chase a championship-winning car for the upcoming regulation era.

Elsewhere, McLaren sticks with its proven duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, despite whispers of brief flirtations between Max Verstappen and the Woking squad. Norris enjoyed a strong campaign with three victories on his way to securing his own world title ambitions, while Piastri looks to bounce back from a tougher second half of the year.

At Red Bull, Verstappen's late-season surge secured second in the standings and solidified his long-term future with the team until 2030. Isack Hadjar proved a reliable benchmark alongside him, earning a sophomore campaign. Meanwhile, Racing Bulls opted for continuity by retaining Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, putting promising junior Nikola Tsolov on reserve duty for now.

Rounding out the midfield, Alpine pairs Pierre Gasly with Franco Colapinto following a marked improvement in the Enstone squad's competitiveness, and Haas locks down its future with Bearman and Rafael Camara. With no vacant seats left, attention shifts entirely to the factories and the long winter ahead.

items.title: Four Practical Ways to Fall Asleep Faster Using Biology
items.snippet: Struggling to doze off? A few targeted physiological hacks—from core temperature drops to deliberate eye movements—can help reset your system.
body: Getting enough quality sleep is foundational for physical and mental performance, yet many everyday factors make it difficult to drift off. Adenosine naturally builds up in the brain the longer we stay awake, driving sleepiness, but variables like late caffeine or stress can block our descent into rest.

Andrew Huberman outlines four actionable, zero-cost mechanisms to help cue the body for sleep. These include manipulating core body temperature, pacing your breathing, shifting cognitive focus, and utilizing specific eye movements to calm active neural circuits.
more: The first strategy focuses on core body temperature. Your hypothalamus acts as a biological thermostat, triggering a drop in core temperature after being exposed to warmth. Taking a hot shower or warm bath signals the body to dump heat effectively, paving the way for sleep. Alternatively, holding something cool can assist.

Second, long exhales until your lungs are empty stimulate the vagus nerve, which naturally slows down your heart rate. This physical pacing is closely linked to heart rate variability and acts as a brake on an overactive nervous system.

Third, tackling racing thoughts requires shifting from conceptual worries—like planning or dwelling on the past—to interoception. By focusing purely on immediate physical sensations at the level of your skin and inward, you interrupt the rumination cycle.

Finally, slow eye movements can induce sleepiness. Moving your closed eyes deliberately from side to side and up and down turns off neural circuits that pay attention to limb position, mimicking the rapid eye movements associated with deep relaxation and rest.
